# BuilderHQ

> BuilderHQ (builderhq.com.au) is Australia's residential construction tendering platform. Homeowners and developers list their project once, with full architectural plans, and up to three verified builders price it on the same scope, so quotes are comparable like for like. Free for homeowners; every builder is ABN and licence checked; never more than three builders per project. Based in Melbourne, operating Australia wide.

BuilderHQ also runs the Preferred Partner register, a hand-picked network of building designers, architects and finance brokers it introduces to owners and builders (no one pays to be listed), and publishes The Build Brief, a weekly briefing on the economics of getting homes built in Australia.

## Platform

- [How BuilderHQ works](https://builderhq.com.au/): list a project with full plans, up to three verified builders price the same scope, compare and appoint.
- [For builders](https://builderhq.com.au/for/builders): tender-ready projects with full working drawings, owners ready to build, never more than three builders per job.
- [For building designers](https://builderhq.com.au/for/architects): the Preferred Design Partner Network, featured and referred at no cost.
- [For finance brokers](https://builderhq.com.au/for/finance-brokers): the Preferred Finance Partner Program, warm introductions when owners ask for finance.
- [FAQs](https://builderhq.com.au/faq)
- [About BuilderHQ](https://builderhq.com.au/about)

## The Build Brief

- [The Build Brief](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief): five minutes on the economics of getting homes built in Australia. Housing starts, building approvals, construction costs, and the decisions that matter. Plain, sourced, every Friday.
- [Issue 005, 7 August 2026](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/issue-005): cancellations of new home sales contracts jumped 50% in June even though sales for the 2025-26 financial year were up 18.4%; from 10 August self-managed super funds can no longer enter new limited recourse borrowing arrangements for residential property, with the HIA estimating 2,415 of 3,613 affected signed contracts will be cancelled; national home values fell 0.7% in July, the largest monthly fall since December 2022; three in four apprentices have never considered leaving; and from 1 July 2027 negative gearing follows new builds only, which a one for one knockdown rebuild is not.
- [Issue 004, 31 July 2026](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/issue-004): the average new private house was declared at $517,430 of building work before land across 2025-26, up 5.0% on the year; annual inflation eased to 3.8% and took an August rate rise off the table, though the trimmed mean held at 3.6%; Victoria's revised Guide to Standards and Tolerances applies from 1 August 2026, assessing finishes from 1.5 metres; and the Productivity Commission's interim report found regulation has become a handbrake on new housing supply.
- [Issue 003, 24 July 2026](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/issue-003): construction costs rose 1.0% in the June quarter as the March lull ended, construction insolvencies fell for the first time in five years (3,435 in 2025-26, down 4.5%, still 24.4% of all administrations), a Melbourne prefab pilot went slab to practical completion in 20 business days, and the BuilderHQ Procurement Standard (BPS) goes to Master Builders Australia for consideration.
- [Issue 002, 17 July 2026](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/issue-002): Victoria's new building rules in plain terms (First Resort Home Warranty, rectification orders, financial standing as a licence condition), Australia as the world's most labour-constrained construction market, and auctions giving way to negotiation.
- [Issue 001, 10 July 2026](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/issue-001): housing starts against the 1.2 million home target, May building approvals, new dwelling construction costs, and how to compare three builder quotes fairly.
- [Australian construction doesn't have a building problem. It has a procurement problem.](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/perspectives/construction-procurement-standard): the BuilderHQ editorial team on why procurement is the one stage of a residential project without a common standard, and the case for the BuilderHQ Procurement Standard (BPS), a proposed framework for structured tender disclosure.
- [Why choosing a builder still comes down to word of mouth](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/perspectives/choosing-a-builder-word-of-mouth): a founder perspective by Moe Akbulut on why Australian residential construction needs a better procurement model, and what fit-based builder selection should provide.
- [RSS feed](https://builderhq.com.au/build-brief/feed.xml)
